10	only at exec time, and rewritten back in the observation that is shown to the
11	model. The model therefore sees an authentic transcript while every episode is
12	fully isolated from every other one. No privileges (no mount namespace, no
13	chroot) are required, which matters on a shared host.
14	
15	Commands run in one long-lived `bash` per episode, so `cd`, shell variables and
16	`export`s persist across turns exactly as they would in a real terminal.
17	
18	`scratch_root` must allow execution -- see `check_exec_capable`. In particular
19	it must not be under `/dev/shm`, which the training image mounts `noexec`.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import asyncio
25	import contextlib
26	import os
27	import shutil
28	import signal
29	import subprocess
30	import sys
31	import uuid
32	
33	# The path every Endless Terminals task (45 of 46) addresses exclusively.
34	GUEST_HOME = "/home/user"
35	
36	# There is no package index reachable from inside the sandbox. Without these,
37	# any `pip install` -- whether the policy types one or a task's setup script
38	# calls a venv's pip by absolute path -- sits in pip's retry loop for minutes
39	# and outlives the timeout that killed its parent shell. With them it fails in
40	# under a second.
41	OFFLINE_ENV = {
42	    "PIP_NO_INDEX": "1",
43	    "PIP_RETRIES": "0",
44	    "PIP_TIMEOUT": "1",
45	    "PIP_NO_INPUT": "1",
46	    "PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK": "1",
47	}
48	
49	DEFAULT_CMD_TIMEOUT = 20.0
50	DEFAULT_MAX_OBS_CHARS = 2000
51	SETUP_TIMEOUT = 120.0
52	SCORE_TIMEOUT = 180.0
53	
54	# asyncio's StreamReader refuses to hand over a line until the whole line is
55	# buffered, and raises `ValueError` once one line passes its limit -- the
56	# default being 64 KiB, which a terminal task reaches just by `cat`-ing a
57	# minified file or a base64 blob. Raise the ceiling, and treat even the raised
58	# one as "this output is too long" rather than as an error: a single episode
59	# printing a long line must never be able to end a training run.
60	SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT = 4 * 1024 * 1024
61	# Stop accumulating output past this. The observation handed to the model is
62	# truncated to max_obs_chars (1200 by default) anyway, so everything beyond
63	# this point was going to be thrown away -- holding it would only let one
64	# `yes`-style command grow a rollout worker's heap without bound.
65	MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS = 1 << 20
66	
67	# Reaping a killed process must not be able to block forever. asyncio resolves
68	# `Process.wait()` only once the child has exited *and* every pipe it was given
69	# has reached EOF, so a background job that inherited the shell's stdout keeps
70	# that future pending even after the shell itself is dead. Several Endless
71	# Terminals tasks ask for exactly that -- one instructs the policy to launch
72	# `sleep 1000` and `yes 'Compiling docs...'` as background jobs -- and it hung a
73	# whole eval at 1199/1200 episodes for half an hour before it was noticed. The
74	# process has been SIGKILLed by this point either way; waiting is a courtesy, so
75	# give up on it quickly and let the object be collected.
76	REAP_TIMEOUT = 10.0
77	
78	
79	async def _reap(proc) -> None:
80	    """Wait for an already-killed process, but never longer than REAP_TIMEOUT."""
81	    with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.TimeoutError, ProcessLookupError):
82	        await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=REAP_TIMEOUT)
83	
84	
85	def check_exec_capable(root: str) -> None:
86	    """Fail loudly if `root` sits on a `noexec` filesystem.
87	
88	    Many Endless Terminals tasks create a script and their verifiers assert
89	    `os.access(path, os.X_OK)`. On a `noexec` mount that returns False even at
90	    mode 755, so perfectly good tasks get silently rejected and any episode
91	    that has to run a script it just wrote fails for no visible reason.
92	    `/dev/shm` is `noexec` in the training image, which makes this very easy to
93	    hit, so check once up front instead.
94	    """
95	    os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
96	    probe = os.path.join(root, f".execprobe_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")
97	    try:
98	        with open(probe, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
99	            fh.write("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
100	        os.chmod(probe, 0o755)
101	        if not os.access(probe, os.X_OK):
102	            raise RuntimeError(
103	                f"{root} is on a noexec filesystem (a mode-755 file there is not executable). "
104	                "Point ET_SCRATCH / --scratch at a directory that allows execution, e.g. /tmp."
105	            )
106	    finally:
107	        try:
108	            os.unlink(probe)
109	        except OSError:
110	            pass
111	
112	
113	def _truncate(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
114	    if len(text) <= limit:
115	        return text
116	    head = limit * 2 // 3
117	    tail = limit - head
118	    omitted = len(text) - head - tail
119	    return f"{text[:head]}\n...[{omitted} characters omitted]...\n{text[-tail:]}"
120	
121	
122	class Episode:
123	    """One task attempt in its own private filesystem tree."""
124	
125	    def __init__(
126	        self,
127	        task_dir: str,
128	        scratch_root: str,
129	        cmd_timeout: float = DEFAULT_CMD_TIMEOUT,
130	        max_obs_chars: int = DEFAULT_MAX_OBS_CHARS,
131	    ) -> None:
132	        self.task_dir = task_dir
133	        self.task_id = os.path.basename(task_dir.rstrip("/"))
134	        self.cmd_timeout = cmd_timeout
135	        self.max_obs_chars = max_obs_chars
136	
137	        self.uid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
138	        self.base = os.path.join(scratch_root, f"ep_{self.task_id}_{self.uid}")
139	        self.home = os.path.join(self.base, "home", "user")
140	        # Marker is per-episode so a command that echoes it cannot spoof us.
141	        self.mark = f"__ET_DONE_{self.uid}__"
142	
143	        self._shell: asyncio.subprocess.Process | None = None
144	        self.setup_ok = False
145	        self.setup_log = ""
146	
147	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths
148	    def to_host(self, text: str) -> str:
149	        """Rewrite guest-visible `/home/user` paths to this episode's tree."""
150	        return text.replace(GUEST_HOME, self.home)
151	
152	    def to_guest(self, text: str) -> str:
153	        """Rewrite host paths back to `/home/user` for display to the model."""
154	        return text.replace(self.home, GUEST_HOME)
155	
156	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- setup
157	    async def start(self) -> bool:
158	        os.makedirs(self.home, exist_ok=True)
159	        setup = os.path.join(self.task_dir, "setup.sh")
160	        if os.path.isfile(setup):
161	            with open(setup, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
162	                script = self.to_host(fh.read())
163	            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
164	                "bash",
165	                "-s",
166	                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
167	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
168	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
169	                cwd=self.base,
170	                env=self._env(),
171	            )
172	            try:
173	                out, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(
174	                    proc.communicate(script.encode()), timeout=SETUP_TIMEOUT
175	                )
176	            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
177	                proc.kill()
178	                await _reap(proc)
179	                self.setup_log = "setup timed out"
180	                return False
181	            self.setup_log = out.decode("utf-8", "replace")
182	            if proc.returncode != 0:
183	                return False
184	
185	        self.setup_ok = True
186	        await self._spawn_shell()
187	        return True
188	
189	    def _env(self) -> dict:
190	        env = dict(os.environ)
191	        env.update(
192	            {
193	                "HOME": self.home,
194	                "PWD": self.home,
195	                "TERM": "dumb",
196	                "LC_ALL": "C.UTF-8",
197	                "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
198	                "PS1": "",
199	                "PS2": "",
200	                "DEBIAN_FRONTEND": "noninteractive",
201	                **OFFLINE_ENV,
202	            }
203	        )
204	        # Never let an episode inherit the trainer's proxy / CUDA context.
205	        for drop in ("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "http_proxy", "https_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY"):
206	            env.pop(drop, None)
207	        return env
208	
209	    async def _spawn_shell(self) -> None:
210	        # Own session/process group, so killing a wedged turn takes the whole
211	        # command tree with it rather than orphaning its children. Over a
212	        # training run that is the difference between a clean host and
213	        # thousands of leaked background processes.
214	        self._shell = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
215	            "bash",
216	            "--noprofile",
217	            "--norc",
218	            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
219	            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
220	            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
221	            cwd=self.home,
222	            env=self._env(),
223	            start_new_session=True,
224	            limit=SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT,
225	        )
226	
227	    async def _kill_shell(self) -> None:
228	        if self._shell is None:
229	            return
230	        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError):
231	            os.killpg(os.getpgid(self._shell.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
232	        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
233	            self._shell.kill()
234	        await _reap(self._shell)
235	        self._shell = None
236	
237	    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- exec
238	    async def exec(self, command: str) -> str:
239	        """Run one shell command; return the observation string verbatim in the
240	        format the Endless Terminals harness uses."""
241	        host_cmd = self.to_host(command)
242	
243	        # A command with unbalanced quotes would hang the persistent shell
244	        # waiting for PS2 continuation, so reject it up front the way the
245	        # upstream harness effectively does.
246	        syntax = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
247	            "bash",
248	            "-n",
249	            "-c",
250	            host_cmd,
251	            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
252	            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
253	        )
254	        syn_out, _ = await syntax.communicate()
255	        if syntax.returncode != 0:
256	            return self._format(self.to_guest(syn_out.decode("utf-8", "replace")), 2)
257	
258	        if self._shell is None or self._shell.returncode is not None:
259	            await self._spawn_shell()
260	
261	        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdin is not None
262	        payload = f"{host_cmd}\nprintf '\\n%s%d\\n' '{self.mark}' \"$?\"\n"
263	        try:
264	            self._shell.stdin.write(payload.encode())
265	            await self._shell.stdin.drain()
266	        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
267	            await self._kill_shell()
268	            return self._format("shell died", 1)
269	
270	        try:
271	            out, rc = await asyncio.wait_for(self._read_until_mark(), timeout=self.cmd_timeout)
272	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
273	            await self._kill_shell()
274	            await self._spawn_shell()
275	            return self._format(f"command timed out after {self.cmd_timeout:.0f}s", 124)
276	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- deliberately broad
277	            # The shell is in an unknown state, so replace it, and hand the
278	            # policy an ordinary failed-command observation. Letting this
279	            # propagate would abort the whole rollout: the eval driver awaits
280	            # every episode through `asyncio.as_completed`, so one raising
281	            # episode discards the other several hundred that succeeded.
282	            await self._kill_shell()
283	            await self._spawn_shell()
284	            return self._format(f"could not read command output: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", 1)
285	
286	        return self._format(self.to_guest(out), rc)
287	
288	    async def _read_chunk(self) -> bytes:
289	        """`readline`, except an over-long line comes back in pieces.
290	
291	        asyncio's StreamReader will not hand over a line until it has the whole
292	        thing buffered, and raises once one line passes its limit. A terminal
293	        task reaches any limit you pick by `cat`-ing a minified file or a
294	        base64 blob -- and the raised exception used to propagate all the way
295	        out of `RolloutManager.eval`, so one task printing one long line ended
296	        the entire run. The buffered data is still readable, so draining it
297	        with a bounded `read` both recovers the stream and keeps the output.
298	        """
299	        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
300	        try:
301	            return await self._shell.stdout.readline()
302	        except (ValueError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError):
303	            return await self._shell.stdout.read(SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT // 2)
304	
305	    async def _read_until_mark(self) -> tuple[str, int]:
306	        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
307	        chunks: list[str] = []
308	        captured = 0
309	        # `_read_chunk` does not promise to return whole lines, so the split
310	        # into lines happens here rather than being assumed. Doing it this way
311	        # also means the marker is still recognised when it arrives in the same
312	        # chunk as the tail of a long line.
313	        pending = ""
314	        while True:
315	            data = await self._read_chunk()
316	            if not data:  # shell exited (e.g. the model ran `exit`)
317	                chunks.append(pending)
318	                return "".join(chunks), 1
319	            pending += data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
320	            while (nl := pending.find("\n")) != -1:
321	                line, pending = pending[: nl + 1], pending[nl + 1 :]
322	                if line.startswith(self.mark):
323	                    try:
324	                        rc = int(line[len(self.mark) :].strip() or 1)
325	                    except ValueError:
326	                        rc = 1
327	                    # Drop the single blank line our printf prepended.
328	                    body = "".join(chunks)
329	                    if body.endswith("\n"):
330	                        body = body[:-1]
331	                    return body, rc
332	                # Past the cap, keep reading -- the marker is the only way to
333	                # know the command finished -- but stop accumulating. The
334	                # observation is truncated to max_obs_chars regardless, so the
335	                # dropped text could not have been shown anyway.
336	                if captured < MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
337	                    chunks.append(line)
338	                    captured += len(line)
339	            # Bound the live buffer too, not only what is kept: `yes | tr -d
340	            # '\n'` emits no newline at all, so `pending` would otherwise grow
341	            # for the whole 20s turn. What is left here is by construction the
342	            # start of a line with no newline in it, so the marker -- which is
343	            # always the first thing on its line -- can only be at index 0:
344	            # keeping the head preserves detection, and the tail dropped is
345	            # mid-line text well past what the observation can show.
346	            if len(pending) > MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
347	                pending = pending[:MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS]
348	
349	    def _format(self, output: str, rc: int) -> str:
350	        head = "Command executed successfully." if rc == 0 else "Command failed."
351	        return f"{head} Output: {_truncate(output, self.max_obs_chars)}\n\n(exit_code={rc})"
352	
353	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- reward
354	    async def score(self) -> tuple[float, str]:
355	        """Run the task's own pytest verifier. Returns (reward, log)."""
356	        src = os.path.join(self.task_dir, "test_final_state.py")
357	        if not os.path.isfile(src):
358	            return 0.0, "no verifier"
359	        with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
360	            test_src = self.to_host(fh.read())
361	        dst = os.path.join(self.base, "test_final_state.py")
362	        with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
363	            fh.write(test_src)
364	
365	        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
366	            sys.executable,
367	            "-m",
368	            "pytest",
369	            dst,
370	            "-q",
371	            "--no-header",
372	            "-p",
373	            "no:cacheprovider",
374	            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
375	            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
376	            cwd=self.base,
377	            env=self._env(),
378	        )
379	        try:
380	            out, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=SCORE_TIMEOUT)
381	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
382	            proc.kill()
383	            await _reap(proc)
384	            return 0.0, "verifier timed out"
385	        log = self.to_guest(out.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
386	        return (1.0 if proc.returncode == 0 else 0.0), log
387	
388	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- cleanup
389	    async def close(self) -> None:
390	        await self._kill_shell()
391	        shutil.rmtree(self.base, ignore_errors=True)
392	
393	
394	def sync_score(task_dir: str, base: str, home: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
395	    """Blocking variant of `score`, used by the offline dataset validator."""
396	    src = os.path.join(task_dir, "test_final_state.py")
397	    with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
398	        test_src = fh.read().replace(GUEST_HOME, home)
399	    dst = os.path.join(base, "test_final_state.py")
400	    with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
401	        fh.write(test_src)
402	    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, LC_ALL="C.UTF-8", LANG="C.UTF-8", **OFFLINE_ENV)
403	    proc = subprocess.run(
404	        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", dst, "-q", "--no-header", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"],
405	        cwd=base,
406	        env=env,
407	        capture_output=True,
408	        text=True,
409	        timeout=SCORE_TIMEOUT,
410	    )
411	    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout + proc.stderr

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Split the admitted Endless Terminals prompt set into train / val / test.
3	
4	A run must train on one set of tasks and be scored on another, and the split
5	must be stable across runs, or a comparison between runs measures the split
6	instead of the change under study. So the split is a pure function of the
7	admitted task list and a seed: run this at any time and you get the same three
8	files.
9	
10	Sizing (defaults) comes from a power calculation for the end-to-end held-out
11	pass-rate claim:
12	
13	  test  300 tasks x 4 samples   Scored *paired* -- the same tasks and the same
14	                                per-task sample budget each time, so task
15	                                difficulty cancels out of the difference.
16	                                With a within-task correlation of ~0.6 that is
17	                                ~430 effective tasks, enough to resolve a 5-6
18	                                percentage-point difference in pass rate at
19	                                80% power. Going past 4 samples per task buys
20	                                almost nothing: at rho=0.6, k=8 is only 8%
21	                                better than k=4 for twice the generation.
22	  val   150 tasks x 2 samples   Used to decide when training has converged, so
23	                                that the stopping point is not chosen on the
24	                                test set.
25	  train everything else         ~1k tasks; at 16 episodes per rollout the
26	                                trainer sees each one about once per 65
27	                                rollouts.
28	
29	Usage:
30	    python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts /tmp/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import argparse
36	import json
37	import os
38	import random
39	
40	
41	def main() -> int:
42	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
43	    ap.add_argument("--prompts", required=True, help="endless_terminals.jsonl from et.build_dataset")
44	    ap.add_argument("--val-size", type=int, default=150)
45	    ap.add_argument("--test-size", type=int, default=300)
46	    # Fixed by default. A split that moved between runs would silently turn a
47	    # within-task comparison into a between-task one.
48	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261009)
49	    args = ap.parse_args()
50	
51	    with open(args.prompts, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
52	        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]
53	    # Sort before shuffling: the input order is whatever the validation pass
54	    # happened to emit, and sorting makes the shuffle depend on the seed alone.
55	    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["label"])
56	
57	    if args.val_size + args.test_size >= len(rows):
58	        raise SystemExit(
59	            f"{len(rows)} admitted tasks cannot supply a {args.val_size}+{args.test_size} holdout"
60	        )
61	
62	    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
63	    rng.shuffle(rows)
64	    test, val, train = (
65	        rows[: args.test_size],
66	        rows[args.test_size : args.test_size + args.val_size],
67	        rows[args.test_size + args.val_size :],
68	    )
69	
70	    out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.prompts))
71	    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(args.prompts))[0]
72	    for name, part in (("train", train), ("val", val), ("test", test)):
73	        path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem}_{name}.jsonl")
74	        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
75	            for row in sorted(part, key=lambda r: r["label"]):
76	                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
77	        print(f"{name:>5}: {len(part):5d} tasks -> {path}")
78	
79	    manifest = os.path.join(out_dir, "splits.json")
80	    with open(manifest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
81	        json.dump(
82	            {
83	                "seed": args.seed,
84	                "n_admitted": len(rows),
85	                "train": sorted(r["label"] for r in train),
86	                "val": sorted(r["label"] for r in val),
87	                "test": sorted(r["label"] for r in test),
88	            },
89	            fh,
90	            indent=2,
91	        )
92	    print(f"manifest -> {manifest}")
93	    return 0
94	
95	
96	if __name__ == "__main__":
97	    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split the admitted Endless Terminals prompt set into train / val / test.

A run must train on one set of tasks and be scored on another, and the split
must be stable across runs, or a comparison between runs measures the split
instead of the change under study. So the split is a pure function of the
admitted task list and a seed: run this at any time and you get the same three
files.

Sizing (defaults) comes from a power calculation for the end-to-end held-out
pass-rate claim:

  test  300 tasks x 4 samples   Scored *paired* -- the same tasks and the same
                                per-task sample budget each time, so task
                                difficulty cancels out of the difference.
                                With a within-task correlation of ~0.6 that is
                                ~430 effective tasks, enough to resolve a 5-6
                                percentage-point difference in pass rate at
                                80% power. Going past 4 samples per task buys
                                almost nothing: at rho=0.6, k=8 is only 8%
                                better than k=4 for twice the generation.
  val   150 tasks x 2 samples   Used to decide when training has converged, so
                                that the stopping point is not chosen on the
                                test set.
  train everything else         ~1k tasks; at 16 episodes per rollout the
                                trainer sees each one about once per 65
                                rollouts.

Usage:
    python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts /tmp/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--prompts", required=True, help="endless_terminals.jsonl from et.build_dataset")
    ap.add_argument("--val-size", type=int, default=150)
    ap.add_argument("--test-size", type=int, default=300)
    # Fixed by default. A split that moved between runs would silently turn a
    # within-task comparison into a between-task one.
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261009)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    with open(args.prompts, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in fh if line.strip()]
    # Sort before shuffling: the input order is whatever the validation pass
    # happened to emit, and sorting makes the shuffle depend on the seed alone.
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["label"])

    if args.val_size + args.test_size >= len(rows):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{len(rows)} admitted tasks cannot supply a {args.val_size}+{args.test_size} holdout"
        )

    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    rng.shuffle(rows)
    test, val, train = (
        rows[: args.test_size],
        rows[args.test_size : args.test_size + args.val_size],
        rows[args.test_size + args.val_size :],
    )

    out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.prompts))
    stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(args.prompts))[0]
    for name, part in (("train", train), ("val", val), ("test", test)):
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem}_{name}.jsonl")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for row in sorted(part, key=lambda r: r["label"]):
                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        print(f"{name:>5}: {len(part):5d} tasks -> {path}")

    manifest = os.path.join(out_dir, "splits.json")
    with open(manifest, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(
            {
                "seed": args.seed,
                "n_admitted": len(rows),
                "train": sorted(r["label"] for r in train),
                "val": sorted(r["label"] for r in val),
                "test": sorted(r["label"] for r in test),
            },
            fh,
            indent=2,
        )
    print(f"manifest -> {manifest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dump every held-out episode's reward, keyed by task, as the eval runs.

slime's own eval logging reports means: `eval/et_test` is the pass rate over the
whole split, and that is all it keeps. A mean is not enough to compare two
training runs here. The two arms are scored on the *same* tasks, so the right
test is a paired one -- per task, did this arm solve it more often than the
other? -- and a paired test needs the per-task numbers, which the mean has
already thrown away. Across a 300-task split an unpaired comparison of two
~6% pass rates needs several times the episodes to reach the same power,
because almost all of the variance between the arms' means is task difficulty
that is identical on both sides and cancels when you subtract per task.

So this hook writes one JSONL row per episode next to the run's other
artifacts. It returns a falsy value on purpose: slime treats a truthy return as
"the custom logger handled it", and the aggregate lines are still wanted.

Wired in by run.sh as
`--custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

# Written by the RolloutManager actor, not by the driver, so the path has to
# travel through the Ray runtime env rather than being inherited from run.sh.
DUMP_DIR = os.environ.get("ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR", "")


def _status(sample) -> str:
    status = getattr(sample, "status", None)
    return getattr(status, "value", str(status))


def _reward(sample, fallback):
    """The scalar reward, whatever shape the sample carries it in.

    slime allows `Sample.reward` to be a dict (`--reward-key` picks a field out
    of it). `data[name]["rewards"]` has already been resolved to scalars, so it
    is the authoritative source; the sample is only consulted if the two lists
    somehow fail to line up.
    """
    if fallback is not None:
        return fallback
    reward = getattr(sample, "reward", None)
    return reward if not isinstance(reward, dict) else None


def log_eval_rollout_data(rollout_id, args, data, extra_metrics=None):  # noqa: ARG001
    """slime hook: `custom_eval_rollout_log_function_path`.

    Returns None so slime goes on to emit its own aggregate `eval N:` line --
    this adds a record, it does not replace one.
    """
    if not DUMP_DIR:
        return None
    os.makedirs(DUMP_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DUMP_DIR, f"eval_rollout_{rollout_id:04d}.jsonl")

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for name, payload in data.items():
            samples = payload.get("samples") or []
            rewards = payload.get("rewards") or []
            for i, sample in enumerate(samples):
                row = {
                    "rollout_id": rollout_id,
                    "dataset": name,
                    # The task directory name, which is what makes the two arms'
                    # rows joinable and the comparison paired.
                    "label": getattr(sample, "label", None),
                    "index": getattr(sample, "index", None),
                    "group_index": getattr(sample, "group_index", None),
                    "reward": _reward(sample, rewards[i] if i < len(rewards) else None),
                    "response_length": getattr(sample, "response_length", None),
                    "status": _status(sample),
                }
                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return None

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.

slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:

    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")

so for the critic the lines look like

    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}

Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:

    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}

Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.

There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

Usage:
    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import sys

STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")

# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")


def _coerce(value):
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
    try:
        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
        return None
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None


def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
                    records.append(
                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
                    )
                    continue
                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    records.append(
                        {
                            "kind": "rollout",
                            "label": m.group("label"),
                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
                            "metrics": payload,
                        }
                    )
    return records


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--warmup-steps",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    records = parse(args.logs)

    critic_steps = []
    for rec in records:
        if rec["kind"] != "step":
            continue
        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
        if hit is None:
            continue
        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
        if value is None:
            continue
        critic_steps.append(
            {
                "step": rec["step"],
                "value_loss": value,
                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
                ),
            }
        )
    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])

    rewards = []
    for rec in records:
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
                coerced = _coerce(value)
                if coerced is not None:
                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})

    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
    #
    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
    response_lens = [
        _coerce(value)
        for rec in records
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
    ]
    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]

    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]

    summary = {
        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
        "warmup_window": len(window),
        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.
3	
4	slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
5	`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:
6	
7	    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")
8	
9	so for the critic the lines look like
10	
11	    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}
12	
13	Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
14	than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:
15	
16	    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
17	    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}
18	
19	Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
20	`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
21	the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
22	stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
23	it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.
24	
25	There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.
26	
27	Usage:
28	    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
29	"""
30	
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import argparse
34	import ast
35	import json
36	import re
37	import sys
38	
39	STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")
40	
41	# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
42	# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
43	# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
44	ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")
45	
46	
47	def _coerce(value):
48	    try:
49	        return float(value)
50	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
51	        return None
52	
53	
54	def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
55	    try:
56	        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
57	    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
58	        return None
59	    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
60	
61	
62	def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
63	    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
64	    records: list[dict] = []
65	    for path in paths:
66	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
67	            for line in fh:
68	                line = line.rstrip("\n")
69	                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
70	                if m:
71	                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
72	                    if payload is None:
73	                        continue
74	                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
75	                    records.append(
76	                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
77	                    )
78	                    continue
79	                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
80	                if m:
81	                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
82	                    if payload is None:
83	                        continue
84	                    records.append(
85	                        {
86	                            "kind": "rollout",
87	                            "label": m.group("label"),
88	                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
89	                            "metrics": payload,
90	                        }
91	                    )
92	    return records
93	
94	
95	def main() -> int:
96	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
97	    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
98	    ap.add_argument(
99	        "--warmup-steps",
100	        type=int,
101	        default=0,
102	        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
103	    )
104	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
105	    args = ap.parse_args()
106	
107	    records = parse(args.logs)
108	
109	    critic_steps = []
110	    for rec in records:
111	        if rec["kind"] != "step":
112	            continue
113	        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
114	        if hit is None:
115	            continue
116	        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
117	        if value is None:
118	            continue
119	        critic_steps.append(
120	            {
121	                "step": rec["step"],
122	                "value_loss": value,
123	                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
124	                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
125	                ),
126	            }
127	        )
128	    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])
129	
130	    rewards = []
131	    for rec in records:
132	        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
133	            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
134	                coerced = _coerce(value)
135	                if coerced is not None:
136	                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})
137	
138	    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
139	    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
140	    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
141	    #
142	    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
143	    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
144	    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
145	    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
146	    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
147	    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
148	    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
149	    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
150	    response_lens = [
151	        _coerce(value)
152	        for rec in records
153	        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
154	        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
155	    ]
156	    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]
157	
158	    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
159	    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]
160	
161	    summary = {
162	        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
163	        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
164	        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
165	        "warmup_window": len(window),
166	        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
167	        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,
168	        "warmup_value_loss_mean": (sum(losses) / len(losses)) if losses else None,
169	        "warmup_value_loss_max": max(losses) if losses else None,
170	        "warmup_value_loss_min": min(losses) if losses else None,
171	        "rewards": rewards[:50],
172	        "mean_reward": (sum(r["value"] for r in rewards) / len(rewards)) if rewards else None,
173	    }
174	
175	    if args.out:
176	        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
177	            json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)
178	
179	    print(f"critic optimizer steps found: {summary['n_critic_steps']}")
180	    if not critic_steps:
181	        print("NO value_loss METRICS FOUND -- the critic never took an optimizer step.", file=sys.stderr)
182	        print("Check that --advantage-estimator ppo is set and that training reached the critic.", file=sys.stderr)
183	        return 2
184	    print(f"{'step':>6}  {'value_loss':>14}  {'value_clipfrac':>14}")
185	    for rec in critic_steps:
186	        clip = "n/a" if rec["value_clipfrac"] is None else f"{rec['value_clipfrac']:.4f}"
187	        print(f"{rec['step']:>6}  {rec['value_loss']:>14.6f}  {clip:>14}")
188	    print(f"\nwarmup window = first {summary['warmup_window']} critic step(s)")
189	    print(f"warmup value_loss mean = {summary['warmup_value_loss_mean']:.6f}")
190	    print(f"rollouts generated = {summary['rollouts_generated']}", end="")
191	    if summary["mean_response_len"] is not None:
192	        print(f" (mean response {summary['mean_response_len']:.1f} tokens)", end="")
193	    print()
194	    if summary["mean_reward"] is not None:
195	        print(f"mean reward (episode pass rate) ~= {summary['mean_reward']:.4f}")
196	    return 0
197	
198	
199	if __name__ == "__main__":
200	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Offline check: an aborted episode must survive slime's train-data builder.
3	
4	`_convert_samples_to_train_data` decides whether an optional per-sample field
5	is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then indexes *every* sample in
6	the batch. So the shape that breaks is a batch mixing one normal episode with
7	one that gave up -- which is exactly what a rollout looks like whenever SGLang
8	aborts a straggler. The failure surfaces as a `KeyError` or a `TypeError` deep
9	inside slime, an hour into a run, and costs the whole rollout.
10	
11	Reproducing that shape here costs seconds. Run it after touching any giving-up
12	path in `et/rollout.py`:
13	
14	    python3 tools/check_abort_path.py    # inside the slime image
15	
16	No GPU, no model and no network: the tokenizer is stubbed out, because the only
17	thing `_abort` wants from it is an end-of-text id.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import os
23	import sys
24	from argparse import Namespace
25	
26	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
27	
28	import et.rollout as R  # noqa: E402
29	from slime.observability.rollout_data_utils import tensorize_rollout_data_for_training  # noqa: E402
30	from slime.utils.types import Sample  # noqa: E402
31	
32	EOS = 151645  # Qwen3's <|im_end|>; any valid id would do, it is never trained on
33	
34	
35	class _FakeTokenizer:
36	    eos_token_id = EOS
37	
38	
39	class _FakeState:
40	    """Stands in for slime's `GenerateState`, which would load a real tokenizer."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self, args):
43	        self.tokenizer = _FakeTokenizer()
44	
45	
46	R.GenerateState = _FakeState
47	
48	ARGS = Namespace(
49	    rollout_top_p=1.0,
50	    rollout_max_response_len=2048,
51	    partial_rollout=False,
52	    use_rollout_routing_replay=False,
53	)
54	
55	
56	def normal_sample(index: int) -> Sample:
57	    """An episode that ran a turn and was scored -- opens every slime gate."""
58	    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_normal")
59	    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
60	    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[10, 11], log_probs=[-0.1, -0.2], trainable=True, text="a")
61	    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[12], trainable=False, text="obs")
62	    sample.reward = 1.0
63	    sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
64	    sample.metadata = {"round_number": 1, "et_task": "task_normal"}
65	    return sample
66	
67	
68	def aborted_sample(index: int, turns: int) -> Sample:
69	    """An episode that gave up -- before generating anything, or after a turn."""
70	    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_aborted")
71	    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
72	    if turns:
73	        sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[20], log_probs=[-0.3], trainable=True, text="b")
74	    return R._abort(ARGS, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")
75	
76	
77	def main() -> int:
78	    failures: list[str] = []
79	
80	    for turns in (0, 1):
81	        sample = aborted_sample(1, turns)
82	        where = f"abort after {turns} turn(s)"
83	        if sample.reward is None:
84	            failures.append(f"{where}: reward is None (slime's eval metrics average over the whole split)")
85	        if not sample.metadata or "round_number" not in sample.metadata:
86	            failures.append(f"{where}: metadata['round_number'] missing (ray/rollout.py:382)")
87	        if sample.rollout_log_probs is None:
88	            failures.append(f"{where}: rollout_log_probs is None (ray/rollout.py:386)")
89	        elif len(sample.rollout_log_probs) != sample.response_length:
90	            failures.append(
91	                f"{where}: rollout_log_probs {len(sample.rollout_log_probs)} "
92	                f"!= response_length {sample.response_length}"
93	            )
94	        if sample.loss_mask is None or len(sample.loss_mask) != sample.response_length:
95	            failures.append(f"{where}: loss_mask inconsistent with response_length")
96	        if turns == 0 and sum(sample.loss_mask or []):
97	            failures.append(f"{where}: an episode that generated nothing must contribute no trainable token")
98	        print(
99	            f"  {where}: response_length={sample.response_length} loss_mask={sample.loss_mask} "
100	            f"log_probs={sample.rollout_log_probs} round_number={sample.metadata.get('round_number')}"
101	        )
102	
103	    # The batch slime actually builds: a normal sample first, so every optional
104	    # field's gate opens on `samples[0]`, then the ones that gave up.
105	    samples = [normal_sample(0), aborted_sample(1, 0), aborted_sample(2, 1)]
106	    for sample in samples:
107	        if sample.loss_mask is None:  # slime does this itself, before the gates
108	            sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length
109	
110	    train_data = {
111	        "tokens": [s.tokens for s in samples],
112	        "response_lengths": [s.response_length for s in samples],
113	        "rewards": [s.reward for s in samples],
114	        "loss_masks": [s.loss_mask for s in samples],
115	    }
116	    if samples[0].metadata and "round_number" in samples[0].metadata:
117	        try:
118	            train_data["round_number"] = [s.metadata["round_number"] for s in samples]
119	        except KeyError as exc:
120	            failures.append(f"round_number gate: KeyError {exc}")
121	    if samples[0].rollout_log_probs is not None:
122	        train_data["rollout_log_probs"] = [s.rollout_log_probs for s in samples]
123	    # These three gates must stay shut: this rollout never populates them, and a
124	    # sample that opened one would take the batch down the same way.
125	    for field in ("rollout_routed_experts", "train_metadata", "teacher_log_probs"):
126	        if getattr(samples[0], field, None) is not None:
127	            failures.append(f"{field} gate unexpectedly open")
128	
129	    try:
130	        tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(train_data)
131	        print("  tensorize: OK")
132	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
133	        failures.append(f"tensorize: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
134	
135	    if failures:
136	        print("\nFAIL")
137	        for failure in failures:
138	            print("  -", failure)
139	        return 1
140	    print("\nPASS: a batch mixing normal and aborted episodes survives slime's train-data builder")
141	    return 0
142	
143	
144	if __name__ == "__main__":
145	    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline check: an aborted episode must survive slime's train-data builder.

`_convert_samples_to_train_data` decides whether an optional per-sample field
is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then indexes *every* sample in
the batch. So the shape that breaks is a batch mixing one normal episode with
one that gave up -- which is exactly what a rollout looks like whenever SGLang
aborts a straggler. The failure surfaces as a `KeyError` or a `TypeError` deep
inside slime, an hour into a run, and costs the whole rollout.

Reproducing that shape here costs seconds. Run it after touching any giving-up
path in `et/rollout.py`:

    python3 tools/check_abort_path.py    # inside the slime image

No GPU, no model and no network: the tokenizer is stubbed out, because the only
thing `_abort` wants from it is an end-of-text id.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from argparse import Namespace

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import et.rollout as R  # noqa: E402
from slime.observability.rollout_data_utils import tensorize_rollout_data_for_training  # noqa: E402
from slime.utils.types import Sample  # noqa: E402

EOS = 151645  # Qwen3's <|im_end|>; any valid id would do, it is never trained on


class _FakeTokenizer:
    eos_token_id = EOS


class _FakeState:
    """Stands in for slime's `GenerateState`, which would load a real tokenizer."""

    def __init__(self, args):
        self.tokenizer = _FakeTokenizer()


R.GenerateState = _FakeState

ARGS = Namespace(
    rollout_top_p=1.0,
    rollout_max_response_len=2048,
    partial_rollout=False,
    use_rollout_routing_replay=False,
)


def normal_sample(index: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that ran a turn and was scored -- opens every slime gate."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_normal")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[10, 11], log_probs=[-0.1, -0.2], trainable=True, text="a")
    sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[12], trainable=False, text="obs")
    sample.reward = 1.0
    sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
    sample.metadata = {"round_number": 1, "et_task": "task_normal"}
    return sample


def aborted_sample(index: int, turns: int) -> Sample:
    """An episode that gave up -- before generating anything, or after a turn."""
    sample = Sample(index=index, prompt="p", label="task_aborted")
    sample.tokens = [1, 2, 3]
    if turns:
        sample.append_response_tokens(ARGS, tokens=[20], log_probs=[-0.3], trainable=True, text="b")
    return R._abort(ARGS, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")


def main() -> int:
    failures: list[str] = []

    for turns in (0, 1):
        sample = aborted_sample(1, turns)
        where = f"abort after {turns} turn(s)"
        if sample.reward is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: reward is None (slime's eval metrics average over the whole split)")
        if not sample.metadata or "round_number" not in sample.metadata:
            failures.append(f"{where}: metadata['round_number'] missing (ray/rollout.py:382)")
        if sample.rollout_log_probs is None:
            failures.append(f"{where}: rollout_log_probs is None (ray/rollout.py:386)")
        elif len(sample.rollout_log_probs) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(
                f"{where}: rollout_log_probs {len(sample.rollout_log_probs)} "
                f"!= response_length {sample.response_length}"
            )
        if sample.loss_mask is None or len(sample.loss_mask) != sample.response_length:
            failures.append(f"{where}: loss_mask inconsistent with response_length")
        if turns == 0 and sum(sample.loss_mask or []):
            failures.append(f"{where}: an episode that generated nothing must contribute no trainable token")
        print(
            f"  {where}: response_length={sample.response_length} loss_mask={sample.loss_mask} "
            f"log_probs={sample.rollout_log_probs} round_number={sample.metadata.get('round_number')}"
        )

    # The batch slime actually builds: a normal sample first, so every optional
    # field's gate opens on `samples[0]`, then the ones that gave up.
    samples = [normal_sample(0), aborted_sample(1, 0), aborted_sample(2, 1)]
    for sample in samples:
        if sample.loss_mask is None:  # slime does this itself, before the gates
            sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length

    train_data = {
        "tokens": [s.tokens for s in samples],
        "response_lengths": [s.response_length for s in samples],
        "rewards": [s.reward for s in samples],
        "loss_masks": [s.loss_mask for s in samples],
    }
    if samples[0].metadata and "round_number" in samples[0].metadata:
        try:
            train_data["round_number"] = [s.metadata["round_number"] for s in samples]
        except KeyError as exc:
            failures.append(f"round_number gate: KeyError {exc}")
    if samples[0].rollout_log_probs is not None:
        train_data["rollout_log_probs"] = [s.rollout_log_probs for s in samples]
    # These three gates must stay shut: this rollout never populates them, and a
    # sample that opened one would take the batch down the same way.
    for field in ("rollout_routed_experts", "train_metadata", "teacher_log_probs"):
        if getattr(samples[0], field, None) is not None:
            failures.append(f"{field} gate unexpectedly open")

    try:
        tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(train_data)
        print("  tensorize: OK")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        failures.append(f"tensorize: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    if failures:
        print("\nFAIL")
        for failure in failures:
            print("  -", failure)
        return 1
    print("\nPASS: a batch mixing normal and aborted episodes survives slime's train-data builder")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

This is the classic **"done hacking"** failure: since emitting done immediately ends the episode with a short response, and most episodes fail anyway...

But wait — emitting done early should yield reward 0, not positive. Why would PPO push toward done? Let me think about the advantage structure: `values` ~ 0.1 initially, rewards ~0.06. advantages = returns - values. With a fresh critic predicting ~0, and mean reward ~2-6%, most episodes have advantage ≈ -value. Hmm.

1	# Adapt from https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF/blob/10c733694ed9fbb78a0a2ff6a05efc7401584d46/openrlhf/models/utils.py
2	# and https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF/blob/10c733694ed9fbb78a0a2ff6a05efc7401584d46/openrlhf/trainer/ppo_utils/experience_maker.py
3	
4	from argparse import Namespace
5	
6	import torch
7	import torch.distributed as dist
8	import torch.nn.functional as F
9	
10	
11	@torch.compile(dynamic=True)
12	def compute_approx_kl(
13	    log_probs: torch.Tensor,
14	    log_probs_base: torch.Tensor,
15	    kl_loss_type: str,
16	    importance_ratio: torch.Tensor | None = None,
17	) -> torch.Tensor:
18	    """
19	    Compute the approximate KL divergence between two distributions.
20	    Schulman blog: http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
21	
22	    Args:
23	        log_probs: Log probabilities of the new distribution.
24	        log_probs_base: Log probabilities of the base distribution.
25	        kl_loss_type: Type of KL estimator (k1, k2, k3, low_var_kl).
26	        importance_ratio: Optional IS ratio (π_θ/π_old) for unbiased KL estimation.
27	    """
28	    log_ratio = log_probs.float() - log_probs_base.float()
29	
30	    if kl_loss_type == "k1":
31	        kl = log_ratio
32	    elif kl_loss_type == "k2":
33	        kl = log_ratio**2 / 2.0
34	    elif kl_loss_type in ["k3", "low_var_kl"]:
35	        # The non negative kl approximation in
36	        # http://joschu.net/blog/kl-approx.html
37	        # Besides non negative, it is also unbiased and have lower variance.
38	        log_ratio = -log_ratio
39	        kl = log_ratio.exp() - 1 - log_ratio
40	    else:
41	        raise ValueError(f"Unknown kl_loss_type: {kl_loss_type}")
42	
43	    # Apply IS ratio for unbiased KL estimation (DeepSeek-V3.2)
44	    if importance_ratio is not None:
45	        kl = importance_ratio * kl
46	
47	    # Clamp only for low_var_kl for numerical stability
48	    if kl_loss_type == "low_var_kl":
49	        kl = torch.clamp(kl, min=-10, max=10)
50	
51	    return kl
52	
53	
54	def compute_opsm_mask(
55	    args: Namespace,
56	    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
57	    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
58	    advantages: list[torch.Tensor],
59	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
60	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
61	    """Compute Off-Policy Sequence Masking (OPSM) mask.
62	
63	    Args:
64	        args: Configuration containing `opsm_delta` threshold.
65	        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample.
66	        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample.
67	        advantages: Advantage values per sample.
68	        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.
69	
70	    Returns:
71	        Tuple of `(opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac)` where `opsm_mask` is a
72	        concatenated tensor of per-token masks and
73	        `opsm_clipfrac` is the count of masked sequences.
74	    """
75	    opsm_mask_list = []
76	    device = advantages[0].device
77	    opsm_clipfrac = torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)
78	
79	    for full_log_prob, full_old_log_prob, advantage, loss_mask in zip(
80	        full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, advantages, loss_masks, strict=False
81	    ):
82	        # Calculate sequence-level KL
83	        seq_kl = ((full_old_log_prob - full_log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
84	
85	        # Create mask: 0 if (advantage < 0 and seq_kl > delta), else 1
86	        mask = ((advantage < 0) & (seq_kl > args.opsm_delta)).float()
87	        opsm_clipfrac += mask.sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
88	
89	        opsm_mask_list.append(1 - mask)
90	
91	    opsm_mask = torch.cat(opsm_mask_list, dim=0)
92	    return opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac
93	
94	
95	def compute_gspo_kl(
96	    full_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
97	    full_old_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
98	    local_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
99	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
100	) -> torch.Tensor:
101	    """Compute GSPO-style per-sequence KL divergence.
102	
103	    Args:
104	        full_log_probs: Current policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
105	        full_old_log_probs: Old policy log-probs per sample (full or CP-local).
106	        local_log_probs: Local (CP-local) log-probs for expansion shape reference.
107	        loss_masks: Loss masks per sample.
108	
109	    Returns:
110	        Concatenated tensor of per-token KL values where each token in a
111	        sequence has the same KL value (the sequence-level KL).
112	    """
113	    # Compute sequence-level KL and expand to per-token
114	    ppo_kl = [
115	        ((old_logprob - log_prob) * loss_mask).sum() / torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1)
116	        for log_prob, old_logprob, loss_mask in zip(full_log_probs, full_old_log_probs, loss_masks, strict=False)
117	    ]
118	    ppo_kl = [kl.expand_as(log_prob) for kl, log_prob in zip(ppo_kl, local_log_probs, strict=False)]
119	    ppo_kl = torch.cat(ppo_kl, dim=0)
120	
121	    return ppo_kl
122	
123	
124	@torch.compile(dynamic=True)
125	def compute_policy_loss(
126	    ppo_kl: torch.Tensor,
127	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
128	    eps_clip: float,
129	    eps_clip_high: float,
130	    eps_clip_c: float | None = None,
131	):
132	    ratio = (-ppo_kl).exp()
133	    pg_losses1 = -ratio * advantages
134	    pg_losses2 = -ratio.clamp(1 - eps_clip, 1 + eps_clip_high) * advantages
135	    clip_pg_losses1 = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2)
136	    clipfrac = torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float()
137	
138	    if eps_clip_c is not None:
139	        assert (
140	            eps_clip_c > 1.0
141	        ), f"The lower bound of the clip_ratio_c for dual-clip PPO should be greater than 1.0, but get the value: {eps_clip_c}."
142	        pg_losses3 = -eps_clip_c * advantages
143	        clip_pg_losses2 = torch.min(pg_losses3, clip_pg_losses1)
144	        pg_losses = torch.where(advantages < 0, clip_pg_losses2, clip_pg_losses1)
145	    else:
146	        pg_losses = clip_pg_losses1
147	
148	    return pg_losses, clipfrac

151	@torch.compile(dynamic=True)
152	def compute_cispo_loss(
153	    ppo_kl: torch.Tensor,
154	    log_probs: torch.Tensor,
155	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
156	    eps_clip: float,
157	    eps_clip_high: float,
158	):
159	    """CISPO loss from MiniMax-M1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13585, Eq. 4-5):
160	    ``-sg(clip(ratio, 1 - eps_clip, 1 + eps_clip_high)) * advantages * log_probs``.
161	
162	    Unlike PPO, the IS ratio is clipped under stop-gradient and the gradient flows
163	    through ``log_probs``, so clipped tokens still contribute gradient. The bounds
164	    reuse the delta-from-1 convention of ``compute_policy_loss``; canonical CISPO
165	    disables the lower bound (``eps_clip >= 1.0``).
166	    """
167	    ratio = (-ppo_kl).exp()
168	    ratio_truncated = torch.clamp(ratio, min=1.0 - eps_clip, max=1.0 + eps_clip_high)
169	    pg_losses = -ratio_truncated.detach() * advantages * log_probs
170	    clipfrac = (ratio_truncated != ratio).float()
171	    return pg_losses, clipfrac

187	class _VocabParallelLogProbEntropy(torch.autograd.Function):
188	    @staticmethod
189	    def forward(
190	        ctx,
191	        vocab_parallel_logits: torch.Tensor,
192	        target: torch.Tensor,
193	        log_prob_keep_mask: torch.Tensor | None,
194	        process_group,
195	        with_entropy: bool,
196	        with_entropy_grad: bool,
197	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
198	        with_entropy_grad = with_entropy and with_entropy_grad
199	        vocab_parallel_logits = vocab_parallel_logits.float()
200	        seq_len, vocab_parallel_size = vocab_parallel_logits.shape
201	        rank, _world_size = _get_vocab_parallel_rank_size(process_group)
202	        vocab_start_index = rank * vocab_parallel_size
203	        vocab_end_index = vocab_start_index + vocab_parallel_size
204	
205	        target_mask = (target < vocab_start_index) | (target >= vocab_end_index)
206	        masked_target_1d = (target - vocab_start_index).clone()
207	        masked_target_1d[target_mask] = 0
208	        arange_1d = torch.arange(seq_len, device=vocab_parallel_logits.device)
209	
210	        def vocab_parallel_softmax(
211	            logits: torch.Tensor,
212	            inplace: bool = False,
213	        ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
214	            logits_max = logits.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
215	            _maybe_all_reduce(logits_max, dist.ReduceOp.MAX, process_group)
216	            # Subtract the max for numerical stability. When ``inplace`` is set, the
217	            # caller passed a scratch buffer it owns, so overwrite it instead of
218	            # allocating another [seq_len, vocab] tensor.
219	            normalized_logits = logits.sub_(logits_max) if inplace else logits - logits_max
220	            # The normalized logit at the target position is the log-prob numerator;
221	            # gather it (a small copy) before the in-place ``exp_`` destroys it.
222	            predicted_logits = normalized_logits.view(-1, vocab_parallel_size)[arange_1d, masked_target_1d]
223	            # Reuse the ``normalized_logits`` storage for exp and softmax so the whole
224	            # softmax costs a single [seq_len, vocab] buffer instead of three.
225	            exp_logits = normalized_logits.exp_()
226	            sum_exp_logits = exp_logits.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
227	            _maybe_all_reduce(sum_exp_logits, dist.ReduceOp.SUM, process_group)
228	            softmax = exp_logits.div_(sum_exp_logits)
229	            return predicted_logits, sum_exp_logits, softmax, logits_max
230	
231	        entropy = vocab_parallel_logits.new_zeros((0,))
232	        entropy_softmax = vocab_parallel_logits.new_empty((0,))
233	        sum_softmax_times_logits = vocab_parallel_logits.new_empty((0,))
234	
235	        def sum_softmax_logits(softmax: torch.Tensor, logits: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
236	            if softmax.is_cuda:
237	                # Avoid materializing the full [seq_len, vocab] product buffer.
238	                return torch.einsum("ij,ij->i", softmax, logits).unsqueeze(-1)
239	            return (softmax * logits).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
240	
241	        if log_prob_keep_mask is None:
242	            predicted_logits, log_prob_sum_exp_logits, log_prob_softmax, log_prob_logits_max = vocab_parallel_softmax(
243	                vocab_parallel_logits
244	            )
245	            if with_entropy:
246	                entropy_softmax = log_prob_softmax
247	                sum_softmax_times_logits = sum_softmax_logits(entropy_softmax, vocab_parallel_logits)
248	                _maybe_all_reduce(sum_softmax_times_logits, dist.ReduceOp.SUM, process_group)
249	                entropy = log_prob_logits_max + log_prob_sum_exp_logits.log() - sum_softmax_times_logits
250	                entropy = entropy.squeeze(dim=-1)
251	        else:
252	            if with_entropy:
253	                _entropy_predicted_logits, entropy_sum_exp_logits, entropy_softmax, entropy_logits_max = (
254	                    vocab_parallel_softmax(vocab_parallel_logits)
255	                )
256	                sum_softmax_times_logits = sum_softmax_logits(entropy_softmax, vocab_parallel_logits)
257	                _maybe_all_reduce(sum_softmax_times_logits, dist.ReduceOp.SUM, process_group)
258	                entropy = entropy_logits_max + entropy_sum_exp_logits.log() - sum_softmax_times_logits
259	                entropy = entropy.squeeze(dim=-1)
260	
261	            local_target_rows = torch.nonzero(~target_mask, as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
262	            log_prob_logits = vocab_parallel_logits.masked_fill(~log_prob_keep_mask, float("-inf"))
263	            if local_target_rows.numel() > 0:
264	                log_prob_logits[local_target_rows, masked_target_1d[local_target_rows]] = vocab_parallel_logits[
265	                    local_target_rows, masked_target_1d[local_target_rows]
266	                ]
267	            # ``log_prob_logits`` is an owned scratch buffer here, so let the softmax
268	            # consume it in place rather than allocating another copy.
269	            predicted_logits, log_prob_sum_exp_logits, log_prob_softmax, _log_prob_logits_max = vocab_parallel_softmax(
270	                log_prob_logits, inplace=True
271	            )
272	
273	        predicted_logits = predicted_logits.masked_fill_(target_mask, 0.0).unsqueeze(-1)
274	        _maybe_all_reduce(predicted_logits, dist.ReduceOp.SUM, process_group)
275	        log_prob = predicted_logits - log_prob_sum_exp_logits.log()
276	
277	        if not with_entropy_grad:
278	            ctx.mark_non_differentiable(entropy)
279	
280	        ctx.with_entropy_grad = with_entropy_grad
281	        # Metric-only entropy still returns values, but does not need the
282	        # full-vocab entropy tensors kept alive for backward.
283	        saved_entropy_softmax = entropy_softmax if with_entropy_grad else vocab_parallel_logits.new_empty((0,))
284	        saved_sum_softmax_times_logits = (
285	            sum_softmax_times_logits if with_entropy_grad else vocab_parallel_logits.new_empty((0,))
286	        )
287	        saved_logits = vocab_parallel_logits if with_entropy_grad else vocab_parallel_logits.new_empty((0,))
288	        ctx.save_for_backward(
289	            log_prob_softmax,
290	            target_mask,
291	            masked_target_1d,
292	            saved_entropy_softmax,
293	            saved_sum_softmax_times_logits,
294	            saved_logits,
295	        )
296	        return log_prob, entropy
297	
298	    @staticmethod
299	    def backward(
300	        ctx, grad_log_prob: torch.Tensor | None, grad_entropy: torch.Tensor | None
301	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None, None, None, None, None]:
302	        (
303	            log_prob_softmax,
304	            target_mask,
305	            masked_target_1d,
306	            entropy_softmax,
307	            sum_softmax_times_logits,
308	            vocab_parallel_logits,
309	        ) = ctx.saved_tensors
310	
311	        if grad_log_prob is None:
312	            raise RuntimeError(
313	                "_VocabParallelLogProbEntropy expected a materialized grad_log_prob. "
314	                "Do not call ctx.set_materialize_grads(False)."
315	            )
316	
317	        grad_entropy_input = None
318	        if ctx.with_entropy_grad and grad_entropy is not None and grad_entropy.numel() > 0:
319	            # In the unmasked path, entropy_softmax aliases log_prob_softmax.
320	            # Build entropy grad before mutating log_prob_softmax below.
321	            grad_entropy_input = sum_softmax_times_logits - vocab_parallel_logits
322	            grad_entropy_input.mul_(entropy_softmax)
323	            grad_entropy_input.mul_(grad_entropy.reshape(-1, 1))
324	
325	        vocab_parallel_size = log_prob_softmax.size(-1)
326	        grad_input = log_prob_softmax.neg_()
327	        grad_2d = grad_input.view(-1, vocab_parallel_size)
328	        arange_1d = torch.arange(grad_2d.size(0), device=grad_2d.device)
329	        target_update = (~target_mask).to(dtype=grad_2d.dtype)
330	        grad_2d[arange_1d, masked_target_1d] += target_update
331	        grad_input.mul_(grad_log_prob.reshape(-1, 1))
332	
333	        if grad_entropy_input is not None:
334	            grad_input.add_(grad_entropy_input)
335	
336	        return grad_input, None, None, None, None, None

371	def get_reinforce_plus_plus_returns(
372	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
373	    kl: list[torch.Tensor],
374	    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
375	    response_lengths: list[int],
376	    total_lengths: list[int],
377	    kl_coef: float,
378	    gamma: float,
379	) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
380	    """
381	    Calculates discounted returns for REINFORCE++ (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03262)
382	
383	    Args:
384	        rewards (Tensor): A tensor of scalar rewards for each sequence.
385	        kl (List[Tensor]): List of per-token KL divergence tensors for sequence chunks.
386	        loss_masks (List[Tensor]): List of response-only loss masks for each full sequence.
387	        response_lengths (List[int]): The full length of each response sequence.
388	        total_lengths (List[int]): The full length of each sequence (prompt + response).
389	        kl_coef (float): Coefficient for the KL penalty.
390	        gamma (float): The discount factor.
391	
392	    Returns:
393	        List[torch.Tensor]: A list of return (G_t) tensors for the
394	                            local sequence chunks owned by the current GPU rank.
395	    """
396	    from megatron.core import mpu
397	
398	    cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
399	
400	    token_level_rewards = []
401	    for i in range(len(rewards)):
402	        local_kl_chunk = kl[i]
403	        total_len, response_len = total_lengths[i], response_lengths[i]
404	
405	        if cp_size > 1:
406	            # Step 1,2:Gather all chunks and token_offsets from all ranks and reconstruct the full response tensor by splitting and placing each part
407	            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import all_gather_with_cp
408	
409	            full_kl_response = all_gather_with_cp(local_kl_chunk, total_len, response_len)
410	        else:
411	            full_kl_response = local_kl_chunk
412	
413	        # Step 3: Compute returns on full response kl tensor.
414	        full_mask = loss_masks[i]
415	        assert full_mask.sum().item() > 0, f"Sequence at index {i} is fully masked."
416	        masked_kl = full_kl_response * full_mask
417	        rewards_for_seq = -kl_coef * masked_kl
418	        last_idx = full_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0][-1]
419	        rewards_for_seq[last_idx] += rewards[i]
420	        token_level_rewards.append(rewards_for_seq)
421	
422	    if not token_level_rewards:
423	        return []
424	
425	    max_len = max(rewards_for_seq.size(0) for rewards_for_seq in token_level_rewards)
426	    padded_rewards = token_level_rewards[0].new_zeros(len(token_level_rewards), max_len)
427	    for i, rewards_for_seq in enumerate(token_level_rewards):
428	        padded_rewards[i, : rewards_for_seq.size(0)] = rewards_for_seq
429	
430	    padded_returns = chunked_discounted_returns(padded_rewards, gamma)
431	
432	    final_returns_chunks = []
433	    for i, returns_for_seq in enumerate(padded_returns):
434	        returns_for_seq = returns_for_seq[: token_level_rewards[i].size(0)]
435	        if cp_size > 1:
436	            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import slice_log_prob_with_cp
437	
438	            total_len, response_len = total_lengths[i], response_lengths[i]
439	            local_returns_chunk = slice_log_prob_with_cp(returns_for_seq, total_len, response_len)
440	        else:
441	            local_returns_chunk = returns_for_seq
442	
443	        final_returns_chunks.append(local_returns_chunk)
444	
445	    return final_returns_chunks

448	def get_reinforce_plus_plus_baseline_advantages(
449	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
450	    kl: list[torch.Tensor],
451	    kl_coef: float,
452	) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
453	    """
454	    Calculates the unwhitened advantages for the REINFORCE++-baseline algorithm.
455	    Broadcasting the scalar (reward - group_baseline) to each token.
456	
457	    Args:
458	        rewards (Tensor): A tensor of scalar rewards, where the group-wise
459	                                baseline has already been subtracted.
460	        kl (list[Tensor]): A list of per-token KL divergence tensors. Used to
461	                                 get the shape for broadcasting.
462	        kl_coef (float): Coefficient for the KL penalty.
463	
464	    Returns:
465	        list[Tensor]: A list of tensors containing the unwhitened advantages.
466	    """
467	    # Broadcast to get unwhitened advantages
468	    unwhitened_advantages = [
469	        torch.ones_like(kl_tensor) * reward_val - kl_coef * kl_tensor
470	        for kl_tensor, reward_val in zip(kl, rewards, strict=False)
471	    ]
472	
473	    return unwhitened_advantages
